messages:
maria_cs: Heads up — HarborView integration tests today show intermittent p99 spikes on /v1/generate during ramp. Baseline: model=m-instruct-7b, steady QPS ~170, p95 ~680ms but p99 sometimes hits ~1.5s. We should propose a low-friction mitigation (quantization + routing) before their next full test tomorrow.
aj_eng: Agreed. Two low-risk moves:
- try an int4* micro-quant variant for short prompts (very aggressive cost wins)
- use prefix-length routing to divert short requests to the compact/quantized variant
Keep the full-precision model as immediate fallback.
*int4 depends on kernel support; fallback to int8 if hardware not supported.
tom_runtime: Also check prefix cache hit rate. If KV cache is low, lots of recomputation drives p99. For HarborView I saw cache_hit=0.18 in the smoke run.
maria_cs: exact logs:
```
smoke/harborview: qps=168 p50=105ms p95=680ms p99=1508ms cache_hit=0.18
```
sophie_customer: If we push int4/quant routing — how much answer drift to expect? Legal/QA require explicit acceptance triggers.
aj_eng: Plan to mitigate QA concerns:
1) run a targeted quality check on HarborView's top-250 actual requests vs baseline (diff + automated heuristics)
2) run a 12h canary at 3-5% with auto-rollback if regression threshold exceeded
3) human review gate if regression > 1% on their blocked queries
We should also attach an eval artifact showing exemplar diffs.
maria_cs: good. I'll request the top-250 prompt samples and their QA pass criteria from HarborView.
tom_runtime: Draft routing policy (Console-friendly):
```
rules:
  - id: short-prompts-int4
    when: prefix_tokens < 32
    route: m-instruct-7b-int4
    percent: 5
  - id: default
    when: else
    route: m-instruct-7b
    percent: 95
fallback: m-instruct-7b
observe: [latency_p95, latency_p99, quality_regression_rate, cache_hit]
alerts:
  - name: quality-regression
    expr: quality_regression_rate > 0.01
    action: rollback-canary
```
aj_eng: Note: int4 requires a quantization-friendly kernel set. If HarborView runs on A10s we should stick to int8 initially. I'll detect GPU family and attach the kernel recommendation.
maria_cs: action items:
- aj_eng: run quick diffs + attach a small artifact (ETA 36h)
- tom_runtime: stage routing policy in Console, add alert hooks and dashboard link (ETA today EOD)
- sophie_customer: fetch top-250 prompt samples + QA checklist from HarborView (ETA tomorrow morning)
sophie_customer: On it. Also HarborView asked if we can do a user-tier routing rule (gold customers get full model). They want predictable latency for their premium users.
tom_runtime: easy to add tier key in rules. Example:
```
rules:
  - when: user_tier == "gold"
    route: m-instruct-7b
    percent: 100
  - when: prefix_tokens < 32
    route: m-instruct-7b-int8
    percent: 10
```
maria_cs: great — we can present two proposals to HarborView: conservative (int8 + prefix routing + tier exceptions) vs aggressive (int4 + prefix routing). Recommend conservative for first canary.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout triggered -> canary_id=canary-4762345890-1, model=m-instruct-7b-int8, percent=5, region=us-west-2
aj_eng: quick eval summary (prelim): p95 down ~30% on perf set, token cost -18%, automated quality heuristics show negligible drift (~0.4% regression). Will share sampled diffs.
maria_cs: perfect. Once HarborView confirms samples we'll run the 12h 5% canary and invite their QA for live review. I'll also add a renewal note: projected cost delta and latency improvements, and that this is a reversible canary.
sophie_customer: HarborView sent prompts + QA rules. They require human review if quality_regression_rate > 1.25% on post-canary window. I'll add them to the alert subscribers.
tom_runtime: reminder: watch rolling windows — if cache_hit rises after routing (more cacheable short prompts), p99 may fall further. Keep an eye on origin server CPU too.
maria_cs: Thanks. I'll collate notes for the CSM renewal deck (ops wins, cost upside, low-risk rollback plan). Will post dashboard link after canary starts. :thumbsup:
